articles.title: Christian McCaffrey Injury Update, Latest on 49ers RB After Missing Action vs. Falcons
articles.summary: San Francisco 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey is not expected to miss time with what the team is calling a mild hamstring strain:
articles.body:
San Francisco 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey is not expected to miss time with what the team is calling a mild hamstring strain:

McCaffrey suffered what was initially referred to as a thigh injury during the first half of Sunday's game against the Atlanta Falcons, but he was able to return.

He initially went to the locker room following the setback:

Although he was getting a lot of work on the sidelines during the first half, McCaffrey did get back into the game in the second half.

McCaffrey finished with 39 yards and a touchdown on seven carries while adding 61 yards on six catches. San Francisco suffered its first defeat of the season with a 29-20 loss.

McCaffrey previously missed time in training camp with what was described as "tightness," although he later revealed that his absence was planned as he ramped up for the 2026 season and ultimately appeared in Week 1.

In six games this year, McCaffrey has rushed for 350 yards and seven touchdowns while averaging 4.5 yards per carry. He's remained a factor in San Francisco's passing attack, hauling in 28 receptions for 190 yards.

The four-time Pro Bowler is one of the NFL's most imposing offensive players when healthy, although injuries have plagued him throughout his career.

McCaffrey was sidelined for the first eight games of the 2024 season with Achilles tendonitis , later appearing in four contests before he was ruled out for the rest of the year due to a PCL sprain .

His injury history goes back further, as he played in just 44 of a possible 68 regular-season contests from 2021-24.

Still, McCaffrey's impact on San Francisco's offense is undeniable. When he was able to play a full season in 2023, he earned First Team All-Pro honors before getting named Offensive Player of the Year.

McCaffrey also received a Pro Bowl nod after suiting up in all 17 regular-season contests during his 2025 campaign.

In 2026, the 49ers hold the No. 1 spot in the NFC West standings with a record of 6-0.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers could get the Super Bowl farewell he wants, yet the Pittsburgh Steelers still have questions to answer
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers has given the Pittsburgh Steelers a reason to believe that his final NFL season could end with more than a playoff appearance.
articles.body: Aaron Rodgers has given the Pittsburgh Steelers a reason to believe that his final NFL season could end with more than a playoff appearance. Pittsburgh’s 16-10 win over the New Orleans Saints in Paris lifted the team to 5-2, keeping its Super Bowl hopes alive. At nearly 43, Rodgers is no longer the quarterback who could carry an offense through every challenge, but his experience still matters. The bigger question is whether Pittsburgh has enough around him to turn a promising start into a championship run. Its defense offers hope. The offense, however, still needs to prove it can deliver when the pressure rises.Aaron Rodgers' Super Bowl dream remains alive as Steelers reach 5-2The victory in Paris showed why Pittsburgh cannot be dismissed as a contender. Rodgers threw a 51-yard pass to DK Metcalf and used his experience to manage key moments, including a third-down scramble that helped secure the win. He also recorded his 540th career touchdown pass, moving into third place on the NFL's all-time regular-season list.Those achievements underline what Rodgers can still offer. Through seven games, he has thrown for 1,699 yards, 13 touchdowns and five interceptions. The numbers are respectable, even if they fall short of his best seasons. His ability to read defenses and make quick decisions remains valuable, particularly when a game comes down to a handful of important plays.Still, the Steelers left points on the field against New Orleans. They scored only one touchdown across four trips to the red zone, a weakness that could prove costly against stronger opponents. Winning 16-10 is useful, but Pittsburgh will need more from its offense if it hopes to survive several rounds of playoff football.Rodgers has already made clear that 2026 will be his final season. That gives the campaign a different feel. A Super Bowl appearance would provide the kind of farewell few players get to choose, especially after a career that has included four MVP awards and a championship with Green Bay. But the opportunity is real only if Pittsburgh can turn its solid regular-season form into consistent performances.Pittsburgh's defense offers hope, but the offense must improveThe strongest argument for a Steelers title run may not be Rodgers at all. It is the defense, which has tightened up at a crucial point in the season. Pittsburgh has allowed only three touchdowns across its last 15 quarters, while its run defense has improved after giving up 4.5 yards per carry during the opening four weeks. Over the past three games, that figure has dropped to 2.8.That progress gives Pittsburgh a chance to win games even when Rodgers and the offense struggle. It also takes some pressure off an aging quarterback who does not need to produce a spectacular performance every Sunday. If the defense keeps limiting opponents, Rodgers may only need to make a few decisive plays.The AFC remains difficult to navigate, with teams such as Kansas City and Buffalo still posing serious threats. Pittsburgh will also need to avoid the offensive mistakes that turn close games into losses. A stronger red-zone attack and more reliable scoring would make its defensive work count for more.For Rodgers, the timing could hardly be more significant. Reuniting with head coach Mike McCarthy has given his final season a sense of purpose, and the Steelers have shown enough to make a deep run plausible. Yet a 5-2 record is a starting point, not a guarantee. If Pittsburgh can pair its improving defense with a more efficient offense, Rodgers may have a genuine shot at one last Super Bowl. If not, his farewell could end well before the stage he wants.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Kayla Nicole slid into Travis Kelce’s DMs after his $44M contract news, TikTok woman claims
articles.summary: Sometimes, all it takes is one comment to change the course of a celebrity love story.
articles.body: Sometimes, all it takes is one comment to change the course of a celebrity love story. And according to one TikTok user, she may have accidentally played matchmaker for Travis Kelce and Kayla Nicole without even realizing it at the time. The woman recently shared a story on TikTok about how she believes she may have helped bring the former couple together. Her claim? She allegedly pointed out Travis' $44 million contract to Kayla in a comment on one of her pictures, and things may have taken an interesting turn after that.How one comment may have changed things for Travis Kelce and Kayla NicoleAccording to the TikTok user's account, Travis was already following Kayla on social media, but Kayla was not following him back at the time. That is when the woman claims she decided to play matchmaker. She said she commented on Kayla's picture, pointing out that Travis had a $44 million contract.The TikTok user believes Kayla may have seen the comment, even though it was later deleted. According to her theory, Kayla subsequently reached out to Travis, potentially setting the stage for their relationship.Of course, there is no independent confirmation that Kayla saw the comment or that it influenced her decision to contact Travis. The connection between the comment and what happened afterward remains the TikTok user's interpretation of events.Kayla Nicole admitted she slid into Travis Kelce's DMsBack in March 2022, Kayla opened up about how she and Travis first connected during an Instagram Q&A. According to TMZ's report at the time, she revealed that Travis had been following her and liking her pictures for months but had not sent her a direct message.Eventually, Kayla decided to make the first move after getting encouragement from a friend and a little liquid courage. She even revealed the opening line she sent him: “My mom says it's rude to stare and not speak.”Kayla also joked about how she approached him, writing, “Slid into that thang like it was third base.” So, yes, Kayla herself confirmed that she was the one who reached out first. That is where the TikTok woman's story comes in. She believes her comment about Travis' money may have played a part in what happened next.Travis and Kayla began dating in 2017 and had an on-and-off relationship that lasted until their final split in 2022. During those years, Kayla became familiar to NFL fans as the sports journalist and media personality frequently seen alongside the Kansas City Chiefs star.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Lamar Jackson Injury Update Provided by Ravens HC amid Latest Rumors on QB's Timeline
articles.summary: Lamar Jackson has missed the last three games with an ankle injury, but Baltimore Ravens head coach Jesse Minter was optimistic about the quarterback's status even though he didn't know for sure whether the four-time Pro Bowler will be available for Sunday's game against the Buffalo Bills.
articles.body:
Lamar Jackson has missed the last three games with an ankle injury, but Baltimore Ravens head coach Jesse Minter was optimistic about the quarterback's status even though he didn't know for sure whether the four-time Pro Bowler will be available for Sunday's game against the Buffalo Bills.

"Lamar's working his butt off to be back and be out there," Minter told reporters Monday. "I think he was able to get in a little bit of work obviously toward the end of last week. So I think he'll be in a decent spot, but we'll know a lot more on Wednesday."

ESPN's Adam Schefter also reported on the situation and stressed the team is "hopeful" its leader will be on the field for such a highly anticipated AFC showdown.

"The Ravens are hopeful he'll be back this week, but the truth of the matter is, only Lamar Jackson knows when he'll be back," Schefter said. "He returned to practice last week in a limited fashion, but just like he missed three games last year at this time with a hamstring injury, he's now missed three games in October with a high-ankle sprain. … But I think everybody's hopeful he can be back in time for Sunday's game against the Buffalo Bills."

Jackson's exact status has been something of a question mark, as he practiced some before Baltimore's game against the Cincinnati Bengals but didn't take the field.

Minter was asked about the overall messaging surrounding the injury since he previously called Jackson "day-to-day" while the quarterback said it was a high ankle sprain that prevented him from running.

"When the player is healthy enough to play, they'll play," Minter said while also reiterating the team will know more Wednesday. "… There's things that change sometimes with injuries and what you think of it right when it happens in a game where the adrenaline and things are still going on."

Tyler Huntley has played for Jackson during the starter's absence and led the team to a victory over the Atlanta Falcons before losing to the Cleveland Browns and Bengals in AFC North games.

Baltimore is now 4-3 overall but 0-2 in the division and in last place.

It likely needs Jackson back and at his best if it is going to be a serious factor in the AFC playoff race, and it seems like his return will be sooner rather than later even if there is still some remaining uncertainty.

articles.title: Travis Kelce's mom Donna Kelce's baby girl confession takes a wild turn as she reveals the unexpected reason behind his name
articles.summary: Last year, Donna Kelce gave Travis Kelce a family story that quickly turned into an amusing moment on the New Heights podcast.
articles.body: Last year, Donna Kelce gave Travis Kelce a family story that quickly turned into an amusing moment on the New Heights podcast. The Kansas City Chiefs star learned that his mother had once hoped for a daughter, only to discover that she had found her own version of one in him. Her playful comments about his fashion sense and dancing left Jason Kelce laughing, but the conversation also revealed a more personal side of the family. From a surprising baby name confession to the uncertainty surrounding her sons’ NFL dreams, Donna offered a glimpse into the moments that shaped the Kelce brothers.Donna Kelce reveals why she once wanted a baby girlDonna’s conversation with Jason and Travis brought back memories of planning her second child. Although she had hoped for a girl, she found plenty to celebrate in the personality of her youngest son. Travis, now known for his confidence, bold style and energetic personality, became the subject of his mother’s affectionate teasing.“I will say, yes, I was hoping for a girl, but I got one. He’s a fashionista… And a dancer,” said Donna.Jason struggled to contain his laughter as Donna poked fun at Travis. The exchange offered a lighthearted look at the family dynamic behind two of the NFL’s most recognisable brothers.However, the conversation took another unexpected turn when Donna explained how she chose Travis’ name. Her inspiration came from a handsome character on a daytime soap opera, rather than a family tradition or a carefully planned naming process.“There was another Travis on a soap opera during the day. Oh my god, he was the most gorgeous man in the whole world, and I named you after him,” she said.Jason was stunned to learn that his mother had kept the real story from his father. His playful reaction added another layer of humour to the confession, while Travis found himself at the centre of a family story he had probably never expected to hear in public.Donna Kelce recalls Jason and Travis Kelce’s NFL journeyBeyond the jokes, Donna also reflected on the difficult road her sons faced before reaching professional football. Talent alone could not guarantee an NFL career, and the family had to cope with uncertainty as Jason waited to learn whether a team would draft him.“Jason was the first one, and I know that that was very taxing. We were all hoping, so desperately, that he was going to get drafted… It went on for days, and it was just one of those things that we didn’t know if it was going to happen, but I knew you guys were talented. I knew you had the perseverance… It’s just that you don’t know how your children relate nationally,” narrated Donna.Her comments highlighted the patience and belief that helped the brothers pursue their goals. She also reminded them that many talented players never get the chance to shine.“There [are] a lot of kids that are talented as you are, sitting on the bench,” Donna said.For the Kelce family, those uncertain beginnings make the brothers’ achievements even more meaningful. Donna’s stories revealed a mother who could laugh at her sons’ quirks while recognising the hard work behind their success.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Rams say they still don't know when Myles Garrett will return from knee injury
articles.summary: Sean McVay said he didn't know on Monday whether Garrett would return to practice this week.
articles.body:
It's been six weeks since the Los Angeles Rams placed Myles Garrett on injured reserve , and they still don't know when he'll return to the field.

Head coach Sean McVay was asked on Monday about whether the Rams would open the 21-day practice window for Garrett's return from injured reserve. Per the Rams website , McVay said he hadn't yet spoken with senior vice president of sports medicine Reggie Scott and didn't know if Garrett would return to practice this week.

Garrett's missed 6 games since struggling in Rams debut

Garrett has been on injured reserve since Week 2 after undergoing arthroscopic knee surgery and was required to miss a minimum of four weeks. Initial reports stated there was hope that he could return after those four weeks. Subsequent reporting shifted the timeline to six weeks. He's missed six games since going on IR, and further updates about his condition and return have been sparse.

McVay was asked about Garrett's status Monday after telling reporters last week that there's "a possibility" he could return to practice this week. That statement coincided with a report from NFL Network's Ian Rapoport that it's "likely that he returns to practice next week." As of Monday, uncertainty remains.

Even when Garrett returns to practice, that doesn't mean he'll be ready to play the following game. Once his practice window is opened, Garrett will have 21 days to be activated to the 53-man roster or be placed on season-ending injured reserve.

The Rams, meanwhile, are in a fight to make the playoffs after starting the season as favorites to win the Super Bowl. They beat the Raiders on Sunday to improve to 3-4 and have winnable upcoming games against the Chargers, Commanders and Cardinals.

Even if they win all three, they'll be 6-4 in a competitive NFC playoff race with one of the league's toughest schedules down the stretch. After a Week 11 bye, the Rams will close their season with games against the Packers, Chiefs, 49ers, Cowboys, Seahawks, Bucs and then the Seahawks again in their season finale.

In short, the Rams don't have much margin for error, and the return of the reigning, two-time Defensive Player of the Year would provide a much-needed boost.

articles.title: Tom Brady's 11-year age gap with Candice Swanepoel raises questions as reports reveal the lengths they went to avoid being spotted
articles.summary: Tom Brady and Candice Swanepoel have reportedly found a way to keep their romance away from the spotlight, but one detail is attracting attention.
articles.body: Tom Brady and Candice Swanepoel have reportedly found a way to keep their romance away from the spotlight, but one detail is attracting attention. The retired NFL quarterback is 49, while the Victoria's Secret supermodel is 38, putting an 11-year age gap between them. Their reported relationship has sparked fresh interest in Brady's personal life, especially as the former Tampa Bay Buccaneers star continues to navigate life after his high-profile divorce from Gisele Bündchen. While the pair have yet to publicly confirm their relationship, reports suggest their connection has been developing quietly for months.Tom Brady and Candice Swanepoel's 11-year age gap puts their reported romance in the spotlightBrady, widely recognised as one of the greatest quarterbacks in NFL history, is entering a different chapter of his life after retiring from professional football. Swanepoel, meanwhile, has built an international career in modelling and remains closely associated with Victoria's Secret.Their 11-year age difference has become a talking point following reports of their relationship. However, the reported romance appears to have attracted attention for another reason: the lengths the pair have allegedly taken to keep their private lives out of public view.According to People, a source confirmed on October 25 that the two have been seeing each other for some time. Their shared home base in Miami has reportedly made spending time together easier.“They’ve been dating for a while now,” the insider confirmed. The source continued, “They both live in Miami, so it’s very convenient. They’re spending a lot of time together.”The reports suggest that privacy remains a priority for both. A second source told People that Swanepoel has been careful about who knows about their relationship.“Candice and Tom have been dating for months. She’s been very secretive and selective about who she’s told about their dating. When they have met up, they’ve gone [to great] lengths not to be spotted.”Neither Brady nor Swanepoel had publicly confirmed the relationship in the reports published on October 25.Tom Brady's reported romance comes amid renewed attention on his Gisele Bündchen divorceThe dating reports have also brought Brady's previous marriage back into the conversation. Brady and Bündchen finalised their divorce in 2022 after years together and share two children, Benjamin and Vivian. Brady also has an older son, Jack, with his former girlfriend Bridget Moynahan.A biography titled Brady: An American Story and the Price of Greatness, written by Lars Anderson, examined the factors that may have contributed to the marriage ending. Anderson reportedly pointed to differences in compatibility and Brady's commitment to football as possible pressures on their relationship.“There was a lot that went into it,” Anderson wrote, according to People.Bündchen has since married Joaquim Valente, with whom she shares a young son. Swanepoel also has two sons from her former relationship with Brazilian model Hermann Nicoli.For now, the reported relationship between Brady and Swanepoel remains unconfirmed. Their 11-year age gap may be drawing headlines, but the pair's determination to keep their personal lives private has become another defining part of the story.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes' $325 million KC Current make history as 18,000 fans turn final home game into a record-breaking event
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes have another reason to celebrate their investment in Kansas City sports.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes have another reason to celebrate their investment in Kansas City sports. The Kansas City Current drew a record-setting crowd for their final home match of the 2026 season, turning the occasion into more than a football game. With thousands of supporters gathering outside CPKC Stadium, the club expanded its matchday experience and brought more fans into the celebration. The milestone also highlighted the growing appeal of women's soccer in Kansas City, where the Mahomes family's involvement in the Current has become part of a wider push to build a strong sporting community.Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes' KC Current welcome a record crowdThe Kansas City Current made history on October 25, welcoming a crowd expected to reach around 18,000 for the club's biggest-attended match. With CPKC Stadium holding about 12,000 people, the team introduced a new Ground Pass experience at Current Landing to give more supporters a place to watch the action.Around 6,000 fans gathered in the outdoor area, where large screens, food, games and family-friendly activities created a festival-like atmosphere. The $10 pass offered access to five viewing screens, a children's zone and halftime entertainment, giving fans another way to take part even if they could not secure stadium tickets.Jocelyn Monroe, the club's chief marketing director, said the occasion was about bringing the city together.“It’s a fun day to come out and celebrate Kansas City and celebrate sports in Kansas City and be a part of history because this will be our largest attended match in Kansas City Current history,” said Jocelyn Monroe, chief marketing director of KC Current.The club also stressed the importance of making its matches accessible to more people.“What really makes the atmosphere is the people, so having more of our fans have the opportunity to come down and build out an accessible area for them is something we always were thinking about,” Monroe said.For Patrick and Brittany Mahomes, who are part of the ownership group behind the KC Current, the milestone reflects the team's growing reach beyond the pitch. The turnout also showed how a match can become a citywide event rather than an experience limited to those inside the stadium.KC Current expands Current Landing with new restaurants and eventsThe celebration brought fresh activity to Current Landing, the entertainment district surrounding the stadium. Two dining options, Revel Bar & Grill and Providence Pizza, added to the area's appeal on an already busy matchday.Providence Pizza marked its grand opening on Sunday, with owner Aaron acknowledging both the excitement and the challenge of opening on such a busy day.“We are excited and nervous. This is our grand opening, so we are opening our restaurant on one of the probably busiest days for Current Landing,” said Aaron, the owner of Providence Pizza.The Current plans to build on the success by hosting more One Current events at Current Landing throughout the year. These gatherings could give supporters more chances to connect with the team outside regular matchdays.For the Mahomes-backed club, the record crowd offers a clear sign of growing fan interest. By combining soccer, food and entertainment, the Current is working to make its home ground a destination for the wider Kansas City community.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Jason Kelce and Travis Kelce’s $200 million Garage Beer rides a 252% sales boom, but a 14-million-barrel rival poses a major challenge
articles.summary: The American beer market has become a tough place for smaller brands, but Garage Beer is finding room to grow.
articles.body: The American beer market has become a tough place for smaller brands, but Garage Beer is finding room to grow. Backed by NFL stars Jason and Travis Kelce, the light beer brand has expanded beyond its Midwestern roots and built a national presence. Its rise is not just about celebrity ownership. A simple product, sharp marketing and a clear understanding of everyday drinkers have helped Garage Beer stand out. With sales climbing and distribution reaching all 50 states, the company is taking on established beer giants in a category where winning shelf space is never easy.Garage Beer sales surge as the Kelce brothers expand their reachGarage Beer recorded a remarkable 252% sales increase in 2023, before the Kelce brothers became majority investors in 2024. That timeline matters because it shows the brand had already gained traction before its biggest celebrity boost arrived.The beer began as a product from Braxton Brewing Company in Kentucky. Its relaunch in early 2023 gave it a fresh identity, with a lighter recipe, new packaging and a focus on just 95 calories per serving. Instead of competing for attention among specialist craft beers, Garage Beer targeted drinkers who wanted an easygoing alternative to mainstream lagers.The Kelces then brought their enormous fan bases and marketing appeal into the picture. Jason's entertaining social media videos, creative promotions and unusual partnerships helped the brand earn attention without relying entirely on traditional advertising.Garage Beer CEO Andy Sauer explained the thinking behind its approach: “I wanted people who were willing to take risks, people who were willing to do something different,” he says. “That’s one of the more monolithic categories in all of grocery. You need people who are comfortable with the idea of very different thinking.”That willingness to experiment has helped Garage Beer build a personality beyond its product. It has also given the brand a way to compete against companies with much larger advertising budgets.Garage Beer faces a bigger test against established beer giantsNational distribution marks a major milestone, but sustaining growth could prove harder than securing attention. Garage Beer is entering a market dominated by established names such as Michelob Ultra, Busch Light and Modelo Especial.The scale of that competition is clear. According to the figures cited by VinePair, Garage Beer expected to produce around 300,000 barrels in 2025. Michelob Ultra, meanwhile, held an 8.2% share of the US beer market by volume, illustrating the gap between a rising challenger and an industry heavyweight.The Kelce brothers provide a valuable advantage, but long-term success will depend on repeat purchases, reliable distribution and keeping consumers interested after the initial excitement fades.Production has also moved beyond Braxton Brewing Company to include partners such as Founders Brewing Co., allowing Garage Beer to meet growing demand.For now, Garage Beer has shown that a smaller brand can challenge established players with a focused product and memorable marketing. The bigger question is whether it can turn celebrity-driven attention into lasting consumer loyalty.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Jonathan Taylor Trade Cost Projected by NFL Insider, Compared to Christian McCaffrey Blockbuster
articles.summary: If the Indianapolis Colts end up trading running back Jonathan Taylor before the Nov. 10 deadline, they may not get a first-round draft pick.
articles.body:
If the Indianapolis Colts end up trading running back Jonathan Taylor before the Nov. 10 deadline, they may not get a first-round draft pick.

But they could get significant draft capital if a past high-profile deal is any indication.

ESPN's Adam Schefter pointed to the Carolina Panthers' 2022 trade of Christian McCaffrey as "the closest comp that we have right now" for what the Colts may get for Taylor. Schefter also said during his appearance on The Pat McAfee Show (3:25 mark), "I don't think they get a one."

The Panthers traded McCaffrey to the San Francisco 49ers in exchange for a second-round, third-round, fourth-round and fifth-round draft pick. McCaffrey was in his age-26 season in 2022, which is similar to the 27-year-old Taylor this season.

Taylor is also at the top of his game having just ran for 1,585 yards and a league-best 18 touchdowns last season. He is also leading the league with eight rushing touchdowns this year.

On Sunday, ESPN's Ian Rapoport and Schefter listed the Green Bay Packers, Seattle Seahawks, Denver Broncos and Minnesota Vikings as teams that "are expected to consider" pursuing Taylor.

A bidding war could drive up the price for Indianapolis.

He also isn't a pure rental considering his contract runs through the 2028 campaign. Given his age and that deal, Taylor should be among the league's best running backs throughout the remainder of his contract and someone who could help any team that traded for him for the foreseeable future.

It just might cost that team a number of valuable draft picks.

articles.title: Adam Schefter Predicts 'Double-Digit' Trades Before NFL Deadline amid Buzz on Jonathan Taylor, More
articles.summary: The upcoming NFL trade deadline could be a busy one.
articles.body:
The upcoming NFL trade deadline could be a busy one.

During an appearance on the Pat McAfee Show on Monday, ESPN's Adam Schefter said he's predicting "double-digit" trades before the deadline on Nov. 10.

"I think double-digit trades from now until the trade deadline is probably realistic," Schefter said (2:09 mark).

Schefter specifically pointed to the Indianapolis Colts as a team that could make a handful of deals, highlighting running back Jonathan Taylor, guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner as some of his candidates to be moved.

Schefter likened a potential trade for Taylor to the blockbuster deal that sent Christian McCaffrey to the San Francisco 49ers from the Carolina Panthers in 2022. He said Indianapolis could likely get a second-round pick and a fifth-round pick for Taylor.

Schefter also noted Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr. and Los Angeles Chargers linebacker Khalil Mack as two of his players to watch ahead of the deadline.

Barring a loss to the Jaguars on Sunday, it's fair to assume the Colts are bound to be sellers at the deadline. Other teams that have had unexpected struggles, like the Philadelphia Eagles or Los Angeles Chargers, could join them.

articles.title: Crazy and memorable stats from Raiders' Week 7 game vs. Rams
articles.summary: The Las Vegas Raiders are on a four-game losing streak. These numbers dictated why they lost at home to the Los Angeles Rams in Week 7.
articles.body:
It's been a month since the Las Vegas Raiders last tasted victory. Since then, they have lost four straight games, including their Week 7 contest against the Los Angeles Rams .

The Raiders fought back by scoring 15 fourth-quarter points. However, Los Angeles' lead was so huge that it didn't matter. Las Vegas' losing streak extends to four games, while the Rams broke a two-game skid.

There's much uncertainty surrounding the Raiders and going on the road for their next two matches might not help their chances to break their slump, either.

But before looking forward, let us look back at the telling numbers that defined the Week 7 Raiders-Rams game.

Matthew Stafford establishes the Rams' franchise TD passes record

The reigning NFL Most Valuable Player torched the Raiders' defense with three passing touchdowns. Those were enough to give him 155 TD passes for the Rams, surpassing 1969 NFL MVP Roman Gabriel for the most scoring throws in Rams franchise history. This milestone also made him the first quarterback to hold the record for two franchises.

What the Raiders will remember, though, is the 21-3 deficit they were staring at with four minutes left before halftime. Stafford found tight end Davis Allen twice and wideout Puka Nacua once to rout the Raiders.

It wasn't even close, as the Rams finished with 199 rushing yards. Blake Corum (93) and Kyren Williams (99) were just a few yards away from having 100 yards each.

In contrast, the Raiders' run game futility continues, generating only 48 yards on the ground. While coming from behind didn't help the run game, it's not the first time that the opponent has shut down Las Vegas' ground attack.

This output has the Raiders averaging a measly 74.7 yards per game, the second-worst rate in the league.

The Raiders only had one successful red zone attempt out of five tries. They had a third-quarter drive that stalled on the Rams' 13-yard line due to an incomplete fourth-down pass from Kirk Cousins to Cody White.

Likewise, they settled for a field goal from the Rams' 10-yard line before halftime. That's a possible 13 points left on the table, which could have made the game more competitive.

No Raiders team has allowed more consecutive games giving up 27 points than the five games the Raiders did it.

Las Vegas allowed four touchdown drives to the Rams in the first half alone, three of which coming in the second quarter, to make it a 28-3 game with 1:30 left until the half. And with that, they tied the record for the most consecutive games allowing at least 27 points in franchise history.

Since this is an active streak, it means that should they give up 27 points to the Jets next week, they would set a new franchise record.

Tre Tucker tied for most deep catches in NFL in 2026

With his 41-yard reception in the game, Tucker now has 4 receptions of 40+ yards in 2026, tied for themost in the NFL. He is averaging 16.3 yards per reception this season, the third highest mark in the NFL among qualified receivers.

articles.title: “Looks Clean to Me”: Cam Skattebo’s Father Calls Out NFL Over Controversial Flag Against Giants RB During Texans Clash
articles.summary: Cam Skattebo’s punishing running style has made him a fan favorite, and his father, Leo Skattebo III, has been one of his most vocal supporters. So when the...
articles.body:
Cam Skattebo's punishing running style has made him a fan favorite, and his father, Leo Skattebo III, has been one of his most vocal supporters. So when the New York Giants running back drew a controversial penalty for lowering his helmet against the Houston Texans , his father had little interest in accepting the officials' decision.

"Looks clean to me," Leo shared his reaction on X on Monday , defending a play that quickly became a talking point among fans and former players.

The post came after Skattebo was flagged for unnecessary roughness during the Giants' 27-21 overtime win over Houston on Sunday. On a seven-yard run in the first quarter, the running back lowered his helmet into Texans safety M.J. Stewart. Officials ruled that he had initiated contact with the crown of his helmet, turning what would have been a productive gain into a costly penalty.

The call also drew criticism from Giants head coach John Harbaugh, who questioned how a runner could protect himself and the football without lowering his body.

"I understand the idea," Harbaugh said on Monday. "You have to run low to protect the football. You have to run low to protect your body. You can't run in there and give tacklers your chest."

Harbaugh added that he did not believe Skattebo was deliberately using his helmet as a weapon. He argued that the running back was trying to lead with his shoulder while keeping himself in a strong position.

Skattebo was equally unhappy with the call. After the game, he said the NFL celebrated his physical running style in promotional content but penalized him for the same approach on the field.

"The NFL loves to post me when I do stuff like that – but then also wants to take stuff from me," Skattebo said. "I'm going to run the ball like I want to run the ball. And if I'm going to continue to get flagged for it or fined for it, man, I guess I'm going to play for free."

His father has supported Skattebo throughout his football journey. Leo coached him during his youth football years and played him at different positions. Skattebo later starred at Sacramento State and Arizona State.

The latest controversy also followed a difficult week for Skattebo. After recording no touches in the Giants' Week 6 game against the New Orleans Saints , he returned against Houston with 124 rushing yards and a touchdown on 17 carries. His performance helped New York secure the overtime victory, though the penalty overshadowed part of his afternoon.

The NFL's helmet-contact rules aim to protect players from dangerous collisions. That includes offensive players who lower the crown of their helmets. The call against Skattebo has sparked debate over how the rules affect physical runners who lower their pads.

For Leo Skattebo III, the decision was clear enough to challenge publicly. His response added to the debate over player safety and the physical nature of football.

articles.title: Packers Place Ex-Eagles Starter & Super Bowl Champion on Roster
articles.summary: Former Philadelphia Eagles starter and Super Bowl champion placed on Packers roster. The post Packers Place Ex-Eagles Starter & Super Bowl Champion on Roster...
articles.body:
There's already been one career resurrection for Mekhi Becton — another could be on the way for the former Philadelphia Eagles starting guard and Super Bowl champion.

"Packers signed Mekhi Becton to the active roster," The Athletic's Matt Schneidman wrote on his official X account on Monday. "Jacob Monk to IR."

"Packers announce they have signed Mekhi Becton to the active roster and placed Jacob Monk on injured reserve," Cheesehead TV's Aaron Nagler wrote on X.

Becton played for the Eagles for one season, spending 2024 as a starting guard on the team that won Super Bowl LIX—a year in which running back Saquon Barkley ran for over 2,000 yards and was named NFL Offensive Player of the Year.

articles.title: Miami Dolphins overreaction Monday: Malik Willis as long-term QB1?
articles.summary: It's an Overreaction Monday. Malik Willis a franchise QB? Ollie Gordon II a RB1? Dolphins to win five games?
articles.body:
The Miami Dolphins beat the New York Jets 28-25 to improve to 1-5.

Miami will host New England at Hard Rock Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 1, at 4:25 p.m.

It's never a bad time for an Overreaction Monday, so ... here goes...

Overreaction? No. General manager Jon-Eric Sullivan has offered some reason for hope with his first draft class. Kadyn Proctor, Chris Johnson, Jacob Rodriguez and Caleb Douglas have often shined. Chris Bell, Will Kacmarek, Kyle Louis, Michael Taaffe and more have shown promise. Sullivan's best-available-player approach is paying dividends.

Miami Dolphins hope for first NFL win at New York Jets

Overreaction? No. The Malik Willis we saw on Sunday is the Malik Willis who flashed at times this summer and as a Green Bay Packer, in limited playing time, too. Malik made smart choices and was dynamic as a runner and made a few impressive off-platform throws. It will important to monitor Willis' improvement from the first third to second third and final third of the season.

Overreaction? No. Miami has only one win. But… they are hitting the realistic goals: relentless effort, promising rookies, positive attitudes, development and improvement, QB showing potential.

Overreaction? Yes. Obviously Gordon is Miami's #1 for the foreseeable future. Obviously De'Von Achane is Miami's #1 at the start of the 2027 season. In a dream scenario Gordon is so good the rest of the way Miami can promote some type of Thunder and Lightning duo, with Lightning still taking most 2027 carries.

Overreaction? Yes. The Dolphins beat the Jets. It's fun but let's not get carried away. Could Miami beat the Jets, Colts and Chargers and finish 4-13? Perhaps. But 3-14 still feels like the most likely outcome. Miami still has 8 stout opponents on their remaining schedule. They'll try to win, as they should, but are still headed toward a Top 4 or Top 5 pick in the next NFL Draft. Which will be important.

Joe Schad is a journalist covering the Miami Dolphins and the NFL at The Palm Beach Post . You can reach him at jschad@pbpost.com and follow him on Threads and Instagram and X at @sc hadjoe. Sign up for Joe's free weekly Dolphins Pulse Newsletter . Help support our work by subscribing today .

articles.title: Eagles vs. Cowboys live updates: Dak Prescott, Dallas dicing Philly defense
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Eagles are facing the Dallas Cowboys in NFL Week 7 action on Monday night at Lincoln Financial Field. Follow along for updates.
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA — Greetings from the press box at Lincoln Financial Field, where the Philadelphia Eagles will take on the Dallas Cowboys in primetime on Monday night.

All eyes will be on the Eagles (2-4) as they look to snap their four-game losing streak against an NFC East rival.

The Eagles and Cowboys will duke it out in a must-win matchup with a gettable NFC East title as the backdrop.

The Eagles, of course, will be without franchise quarterback Jalen Hurts, who is expected to miss the rest of the season with blood clots in his lungs.

Tanner McKee will make his second straight start, and he'll do so without wide receivers DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks. But running back Saquon Barkley and left guard Landon Dickerson are back, which should help.

We'll see how the Eagles fare on a night when owner Jeffrey Lurie is being inducted into the team's Hall of Fame.

Follow along for real-time updates from the Linc.

George Pickens' beautiful, 21-yard touchdown catch in the back of the end zone was hard for any DB to guard against. But the Eagles' defense is getting diced up right now. The defensive line is getting washed away on the ground. And Dak Prescott has enough time, especially on play-action, to find his guys. Just not good enough from Vic Fangio's unit.

For weeks we watched the Eagles' offense hang the defense out to dry. In the first half, we're seeing the inverse.

After what might have been the offense's best quarter of the season, the Eagles kickstart the second quarter with a Dameon Pierce touchdown run. Pierce's five-yard burst into the end zone capped a 13-play, 76-yard march.

This Dallas defense is bad, that's for sure. But Sean Mannion's offense looks far more varied and creative through two drives than it has in recent weeks. Credit to Mannion and the rest of the staff for a solid plan so far.

Something to monitor: it's clear Saquon Barkley is managing his hamstring injury. He's come off the field gingerly a couple times. Barkley hasn't been looked at by trainers. But the superstar RB appears to be on a bit of a pitch count.

We've got a high-scoring affair early. Dallas answered Saquon Barkley's touchdown with a red-zone TD strike to Ceedee Lamb, who beat Cooper DeJean one-on-one.

The Eagles had a chance to get off the field, forcing a third-and-8 early on Dallas' drive. But a 35-yard connection from Dak Prescott to Ryan Flournoy kept the drive alive.

Saquon Barkley is back in a big way. The Eagles' star running back dominated on his first drive back in action after missing most of the last three weeks with a hamstring injury.

Barkley touched the ball three times — a 12-yard catch, a 29-yard run and an eight-yard TD run. There was also a key 21-yard catch and run by Makai Lemon in there as the Eagles popped Dallas in the mouth with a 75-yard TD drive.

Huge statement early on from the Eagles' offense.

Dallas gets on the board first with a 55-yard field goal by Brandon Aubrey. The Cowboys had an opportunity to accept an illegal formation penalty and go for it on fourth-and-3, but they decided to take the points. We'll see if that plays a factor later on.

In addition to Dickerson, the Eagles will also have center Drew Kendall back . A reinforced offensive line should be able to open holes for Barkley against Dallas, the NFL's worst run defense. If it doesn't happen tonight, it won't happen.

Joe Milton will be the backup quarterback with rookie Cole Payton serving as the emergency QB3. Milton was on the Cowboys' practice squad as recently as last week. Now, he's one injury away from facing his old team. We talked to Milton about his decision to join the Eagles.

Rookie tight end Eli Stowers, who was activated off the IR, is set to make his NFL debut . He had a rough preseason. But can he showcase the athleticism that gave Howie Roseman the confidence to take him No. 54 overall?

Edge rushers Jonathan Greenard and Jalyx Hunt are both active. They'll be playing hurt, realizing the Eagles need them in some capacity to pressure Dak Prescott. How much of a pitch count will Greenard and Hunt be on, if any?
